fields.title: Radiotherapy in Israel as the principal method of treating cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Earlier methods of radiotherapy involved irradiating the diseased area with high doses of radiation energy. Under the strong beam, the tumour processes were destroyed. The destructive effect, however, also reached neighbouring healthy tissue, which led to complications.

Modern radiation technologies using linear accelerator particles are designed to affect healthy cells as little as possible while acting more powerfully on cancer cells. Even so, this design of irradiator is not the last word in medicine.

Despite the results already achieved, Israeli scientists work constantly on improving treatment methods and the technical characteristics of medical equipment. Their contribution to modern engineering is already plain to see.

Until recently the three-dimensional radiation system was a revolution in medicine. Today Israeli engineers have developed a four-dimensional format of irradiation. The newest development makes it possible to treat hard-to-reach, mobile tumours that move to their own rhythm, shifting the focus of the disease.

The new system is built so that the patient need not hold their breath during a session of irradiation. The equipment can locate the tumour precisely and change the direction of the beams by itself as the tumour moves.

Scientists consider this technique the most effective of those available and regard it as the one method capable of defeating cancer. Judging by the many reports, the technology rules out errors and side effects and does not damage neighbouring organs and tissue. What is more, because the dose is higher, the number of sessions and their length are considerably reduced, which allows the patient to recover sooner and makes the procedure available to a greater number of patients.

fields.title: Cancer is afraid of a healthy lifestyle
fields.bodyHtml:
We are told about the benefits of a healthy lifestyle, but few people keep to one.

A healthy lifestyle means more than giving up alcohol and nicotine. It includes a proper diet, regular physical activity, a sensible working pattern, rest and much else. But the question arises: how does all this affect the development of cancer?

A large number of cancer cases are linked precisely to an unhealthy lifestyle and to environmental factors rather than to genetic causes, in the view of scientists at Arizona State University in the United States.

The experts analysed twelve studies examining the link between lifestyle and death from cancer. The participants ranged in age from 25 to 79.

It was established that when cancer prevention recommendations were followed, the risk of developing the disease fell from 10 to 45 per cent, and the likelihood of death from 14 to 6 per cent. The incidence of breast cancer fell from 60 to 19 per cent, of endometrial cancer from 60 to 23 per cent, and of bowel cancer from 52 to 27 per cent.

Dr Lindsay Kohler, the author of the new study, said: «Failure to follow a proper diet, lack of physical activity, alcohol consumption and smoking are the cause of the disease in more than 20 per cent of cases, so by changing one's way of life one can reduce the likelihood of illness.»

It follows from these figures that one cancer patient in five brought the malignancy upon themselves.

Original source: 9tv.co.il

fields.title: Once and for all: which free tests in Israel save people from cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Early diagnosis improves the outlook for survival, and even for a full recovery

At what age should a woman have a mammogram? What is the difference between a colonoscopy and a faecal occult blood test? Can fifty diseases be detected by a simple blood test? Which examinations make it possible to find tumours at an early stage and save a life? Let us look at each in turn.
Early diagnosis of cancer of the cervix
In 99 per cent of cases cervical cancer is caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV), which is transmitted sexually. There is now an examination that looks for the DNA of this virus (HPV DNA). If the results call for further investigation, a PAP smear is taken. The combination of these two diagnostic methods makes it possible to detect precancerous changes in the cervix. The Ministry of Health recommends that women aged 25 to 65 have a cervical smear once every three years, or as directed by their doctor. Sadly, only 50 per cent of women in that age group attend for this examination.
Early diagnosis of breast cancer
The well-known screening examination that makes it possible to find a tumour at an early stage is mammography. For women with no family history of the disease and no particular risk factors, mammography is recommended between the ages of 35 and 74, once every two years. A mammogram is a quick X-ray of the breast tissue. It makes it possible to detect growths in the breast at a very early stage, when they still cannot be felt. Take-up of mammography is higher than for other screening examinations. Awareness of the procedure has grown in recent years, but not all women come forward, and there are groups of the population where the proportion who do is very low.
Detecting breast tumours early saves the lives of women in 90 per cent of cases or more.
Early diagnosis of lung cancer. Many methods of treating this disease have been developed in recent years, particularly at the early stages, so early diagnosis considerably improves the chances of survival. At present, in most patients the tumour is found only once it has already spread.
From 2022 the Ministry of Health, together with the health funds, began a trial of early lung cancer diagnosis. This is an examination based on low-dose computed tomography (CT) of the chest. It is intended for smokers, or for those who previously smoked a packet of cigarettes a day for twenty years or two packets a day for ten. It should be noted that an important measure for preventing lung cancer, as for a number of other tumours, is giving up smoking.
Early diagnosis of bowel cancer. Among the important forms of examination is the faecal occult blood test. This simple examination can save a life. Hidden bleeding is often the first symptom of an early-stage bowel tumour. Finding precancerous growths (polyps) in the bowel makes it possible to remove them before they turn malignant. It is important to remember that early diagnosis of bowel cancer considerably improves the likelihood of a cure. The Ministry of Health recommends this examination for people aged 40 to 74 who have no additional risk factors. In certain cases — where there is polyposis, inflammatory bowel disease, or first-degree relatives (parents, siblings, children) with a bowel tumour — a colonoscopy is recommended, which allows examination of the rectum and the rest of the bowel. A flexible tube with a camera at the end is passed into the bowel through the anus. This examination is not recommended for the population as a whole: it is considered invasive and requires preparation. Take-up of early bowel cancer diagnosis stands at only 66 to 68 per cent.
According to the Israel Cancer Association, a third of those with a positive faecal occult blood test do not follow it up with a colonoscopy, which raises their risk of developing a bowel tumour, and of dying from it, by tens of per cent. Delaying a colonoscopy after occult blood has been found in the stool raises both the risk of the disease itself and the risk of a fatal outcome: a delay of two months by 33 per cent, a delay of a year by 66 per cent.

fields.title: A new type of vaccine has been developed that is capable of defeating any disease
fields.bodyHtml:
The Massachusetts Institute of Technology has developed a new type of vaccine that can be adapted within a short time to fight any epidemic.

As reported in a paper published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the scientists obtained antigens against the agents of Ebola, swine flu and toxoplasmosis, among others. Their effectiveness approaches 100 per cent.

The method consists in «programming» the structure of messenger RNA to synthesise proteins that activate the immune system to fight a particular disease. As the means of delivering the RNA structure into the cell, the scientists propose using nanoparticles.

RNA-type vaccines can be given intramuscularly. So far they have been tested successfully in mice. A series of experiments recorded resistance to the Ebola virus, swine flu and toxoplasmosis in the laboratory mice.

The scientists note that RNA vaccines are less harmful than conventional DNA vaccines, since they do not alter the genome of the cells and do not lead to subsequent mutations.

Original source: 9tv.co.il
